title: 11 Must‑Watch Free‑Agent Targets Shaking Up MLB’s Upcoming Season
body:
The clock struck 5 p.m. Eastern on Friday, and with it came a cascade of roster moves that reshaped the upcoming free‑agent market. Teams that held contractual rights to players for the 2027 season either extended offers or opted to “non‑tender” them, instantly turning those athletes into unrestricted free agents. Eleven of the newly available players stood out for their blend of proven production, untapped upside, and the potential to fill immediate holes for clubs looking to bolster depth before the next offseason frenzy.

Among the most talked‑about names is right‑handed reliever **Jared “The Jet” Ramirez**, who posted a 2.31 ERA over 71 innings last season with a 12‑5 save record for a mid‑market team that missed the playoffs. His high‑velocity fastball (averaging 97 mph) and a sharp slider have made him a coveted asset for any bullpen seeking a late‑inning closer or set‑up man. Ramirez’s market value is likely to hover in the $7‑9 million range for a one‑year deal, though teams with deeper pockets could tempt him with a multi‑year pact that includes a club option.

Another intriguing free agent is **outfielder/first‑baseman Keegan Liu**, a 27‑year‑old who posted a .285/.360/.508 slash line with 28 home runs and 92 RBIs in 2026. Liu’s blend of power and plate discipline makes him a rare commodity in today’s game, where many clubs prioritize on‑base skills over raw slugging. The left‑handed hitter could fit seamlessly into a lineup that lacks consistent run production, and his defensive versatility—capable of handling both corner outfield spots and first base—adds to his appeal. Analysts project Liu could command a contract in the $12‑15 million range for a two‑year term.

The list also includes **young pitcher Tyler “Turbo” McAllister**, a 23‑year‑old lefty who struggled with consistency in 2026, posting a 5.12 ERA across 22 starts. Despite the numbers, his underlying metrics—particularly a 3.8 K/9 and a spin rate that ranks in the top 10 percent of the league—suggest a ceiling that many teams find hard to ignore. If a club can refine his mechanics and provide a stable role, McAllister could evolve into a frontline starter. Expect interest from rebuilding franchises willing to gamble on potential, possibly offering a modest three‑year, $9‑million contract with performance incentives.

Veteran catcher **Luis “The Wall” Ortega** also entered free agency after being non‑tendered. Ortega’s career has been defined by his defensive prowess—he leads active catchers in framing runs saved and has a reputation for handling pitching staffs with poise. Offensively, he posted a modest .240 average with 8 home runs, but his value lies in his ability to manage games and mentor younger pitchers. In a market where quality catchers are scarce, Ortega could secure a one‑year, $4 million deal with a club seeking a steady presence behind the plate, especially those with emerging young arms.

A surprise inclusion is **utility infielder Marco Alvarez**, who saw limited action last season but demonstrated a knack for clutch hitting, batting .310 in high‑leverage situations. His defensive flexibility—capable of covering second, short, and third—makes him an attractive depth piece for playoff‑contending teams that need insurance against injuries. Alvarez’s modest service time suggests a contract in the $2‑3 million range, likely on a one‑year basis with an option for a second year.

The broader implications of Friday’s non‑tender decisions are significant. Teams that chose to cut ties did so primarily to preserve payroll flexibility and avoid arbitration battles that could inflate salaries beyond projected value. By releasing players like Ramirez and Liu, clubs signal a willingness to reallocate resources toward younger talent or to pursue high‑impact free agents in the upcoming July market. Conversely, teams that retained their players—most notably those who extended qualifying offers—demonstrate confidence in their developmental pipelines and a desire to maintain continuity.

Looking ahead, the free‑agent pool will continue to evolve as the trade deadline approaches and as clubs assess their postseason prospects. The eleven players highlighted here represent a microcosm of the market’s diversity: proven veterans, high‑upside youngsters, and versatile role players. Their next destinations will be dictated not only by contract dollars but also by strategic fit, clubhouse chemistry, and each organization’s timeline. As spring training looms, the decisions made in the coming weeks will set the tone for the 2027 season
